implementation.compatibility: InteractionMixin inherits PromptsMixin; interaction imports re-export existing public types/helpers. No cli.py, static/, top-level export or streaming edits.
implementation.write_path: Every response calls the existing send_events; no second transport.
implementation.legacy_permission: cli_permission_response delegates to cli_permission_decision, retaining original request ID and putting toolUseID inside the decision.
implementation.legacy_dialog: cli_dialog_response now delegates to the authoritative behavior=completed/cancelled builder, not the old status field.
implementation.upstream_reuse: Extends the existing fork and captured browser/worker contracts. Prior-art evaluation is in the research handoff; no additional framework or alternate client introduced.

integration_contract.imports: from claude_rc.prompts import PendingRequest, Question, QuestionOption, PromptsMixin, build_answers, find_pending, pending_from_initialize
integration_contract.pending: pending_requests(session_id, *, limit=200, initialize=False, initialized=None) -> list[PendingRequest]. limit is page size, not history cutoff. initialize=True reconciles full paged history with a fresh authoritative worker snapshot. Default remains read-only. A supplied earlier snapshot is seeded then settled by response/cancellation IDs from history.
integration_contract.questions: answer_questions(session_id, request, selections=None, *, other=None, skipped=(), notes=None, previews=None, unanswered=None, unanswered_encoding="worker") -> dict. All keyed inputs accept question text, unique header or zero-based index. unanswered values: skipped/dismissed/replied_in_chat.
integration_contract.browser_semantics: unanswered_encoding="browser" inserts exact browser sentinel strings; worker encoding leaves unanswered values absent and only annotates. These are not equivalent. UI should deliberately choose browser encoding.
integration_contract.convenience: skip_questions/dismiss_questions/questions_replied_in_chat(session_id, request, *, encoding="worker"). Browser parity callers pass encoding="browser". questions_replied_in_chat does NOT send the chat text; send_prompt separately, as live-verified.
integration_contract.question_fields: Question.kind, description, placeholder, number_constraints expose captured optional fields. number_constraints preserves min/max/step/defaultValue/unit without fabricating missing values. Numeric Other values validate finite decimal/min/max/step. Original raw question/input fields are retained, including future fields.
integration_contract.permissions: allow_once(session_id, request, *, updated_input=None); always_allow(session_id, request, *, permissions=None, updated_input=None); deny_permission(session_id, request, message=..., *, interrupt=None). Exact caller rules or request suggestions only; no invented broad always-allow rules.
integration_contract.dialogs: answer_dialog(session_id, request, *, completed=True, result=None); answer_elicitation(session_id, request, action="accept", content=None); answer_hook_callback(session_id, request, output). Typed PendingRequest inputs reject mismatched subtypes.
integration_contract.renderers: No supportedDialogKinds advertised: codecs are not renderers. Integration must advertise only dialog kinds it actually renders.
integration_contract.cli: No registration/dispatch edits are needed for existing pending/answer CLI entrypoints: their legacy imports continue to work. Group08 owns adding preview/notes/unanswered-encoding flags and browser sentinel selection in the panel.
integration_contract.breaking_wire_corrections: Updated two old test_client assertions for toolUseID placement and dialog behavior key; all public method call signatures remain compatible.

checks.name: four_card_continuation
checks.text:
The acceptance test ran. Values as returned:

- **Colour?** = `Blue`
- **Blue preview annotation:** `blue preview notes: acceptance note`. This is what came back as the selected preview. The preview I supplied was "Blue: a primary colour, commonly associated with calm and trust."
- **Toppings?** = `Ham,Egg` (multi-select)
- **Name?** = `Ada`. Free text wasn't supported by the schema, so this was a two-option question (Name A / Name B). `Ada` is a value that wasn't among my options.
- **Count?** = `3`. Numeric input wasn't supported, so this was a two-option question (1 item / 2 items). `3` is also outside my options.

The schema only admits single- and multi-select options, so the free-text and numeric fields were approximated. Name and Count accepted values outside the offered options. No other tools were used.
